translationRepairs: Under the Taizong he was styled the "Fourth Beile"; because Qi Chongge was well versed in letters and history, he was put in charge of secretarial work.
When the Taizong was still styled the "Fourth Beile," because Qi Chongge was well versed in letters and history, he was put in charge of secretarial work.
太宗時號「四貝勒」attributes 四貝勒 to Taizong, not Qi Chongge; the original wrongly styles Qi Chongge the Fourth Beile. The proposed fix is right in referent but the bracketed [still] is not natural English.
In the Taizong's time he was styled the "Fourth Beile"; because Qi Chongge was skilled in letters and history, he was ordered to manage secretarial work.
In the time when the Taizong was styled the "Fourth Beile," because Qi Chongge was skilled in letters and history, he was ordered to manage secretarial work.
Same referent error in the literal: 四貝勒 names Taizong; the proposed temporal clause correctly attaches the style to him, not to Qi Chongge.

Qi Chongge, for failing to advise Prince Hooge to join the emperor in escorting the army and for privately visiting his estate that same day, was liable to death; the sentence was commuted—he was stripped of office, had his ears pierced and was flogged, and was placed under the Prince Regent.

Qi Chongge, for failing to advise Prince Yu Dodo to join the emperor in escorting the army and for privately visiting his estate that same day, was liable to death; the sentence was commuted—he was stripped of office, had his ears pierced and was flogged, and was placed under the Prince Regent.
不啟豫親王多鐸 names Prince Yu Dodo; rendering him as Prince Hooge is a clear misidentification.

Qi Chongge, for not advising Prince Hooge Dotuo to accompany the emperor in escorting him and on that same day privately going to his estate, was liable to death; the order was to show leniency—he was stripped of office, had his ears pierced and was whipped, and was placed under the Prince Regent.

Qi Chongge, for not advising Prince Yu Dodo to accompany the emperor in escorting him and on that same day privately going to his estate, was liable to death; the order was to show leniency—he was stripped of office, had his ears pierced and was whipped, and was placed under the Prince Regent.
Literal likewise misreads 豫親王多鐸 as Prince Hooge Dotuo; Prince Yu Dodo is the correct person.
In the sixth year he was given the added titles of Junior Tutor and Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
In the sixth year he was given the added titles of Junior Tutor and Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
太子太傅 is Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent; Junior Preceptor would be 少師, so the original under-ranks 太傅.
Soon he was given the added titles of Junior Preceptor and Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
Soon he was given the added titles of Junior Preceptor and Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
太子太師 is Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent; Junior Tutor understates 太師.
In Shunzhi 1 he was restored to his former office and rose in succession to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and concurrent Chancellor of the Imperial Academy.
In Shunzhi 1 he was restored to his former office and rose in succession to Junior Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent and concurrent Chancellor of the Imperial Academy.
少詹事 is Junior Supervisor in the Household of the Heir Apparent (詹事府), confirmed by the next unit's 詹事府裁; it is not 太子太保/Junior Guardian.
In the first year of Shunzhi he was restored to his former office and was repeatedly promoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, concurrently Chancellor of the Imperial Academy.

In the first year of Shunzhi he was restored to his former office and was repeatedly promoted to Junior Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent, concurrently Chancellor of the Imperial Academy.
Same 少詹事 mistranslation in the literal; the Household office sense is required.
If Mingxia were again condemned, that would be untrustworthy."
If Mingxia were condemned again, that would make me untrustworthy."
是為不信 in the emperor's speech means condemning Mingxia again would make the speaker himself untrustworthy; the original literal drops that first-person consequence.
Censor Yang Yi discussed ministry recommendations that skipped proper order; Zhengzong argued with him and the two clung to each other in mutual abuse.
Censor Yang Yi discussed ministry recommendations that skipped proper order; Zhengzong argued with him and they stubbornly exchanged mutual abuse.
執相詬詈 means they persisted in mutual abuse, not that they physically clung together; the proposed wording restores that sense.
he also stated that Zhilin had prompted Minister of Rites Hu Shi'an to recommend Prefect Shen Lingshi, who was soon memorialized against by Governor Li Huizu—this was evidence of faction forming.

總督 is Governor-General, distinct from 巡撫 usually rendered Governor; the replacement corrects the office rank.
